section_summary: This section contains translated transcripts of Japanese station JZI broadcasts from November and December 1941, with two Federal Bureau of Investigation cover letters forwarding groups of transcripts to the State Department. The November programs report Diet speeches, economic and military mobilization, and the deteriorating Japanese-American negotiations; the December program reports Japanese attacks on Hong Kong and elsewhere. The November 22 broadcast appears three times as separate copies.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 17, 1941
subfiles.about: Reports speeches at the Diet emergency session and related military and evacuation news.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes Tojo's and Togo's statements on East Asia, the Axis alliance, and talks with the United States, then Kaya's account of wartime finances. It also reports Japanese operations in China and the Taiyo Maru's arrival in Yokohama.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 18, 1941
subfiles.about: Covers reactions to Diet speeches, Japanese-American talks, and support for overseas Japanese.
subfiles.summary: Reports reactions in Berlin, Washington, Nanjing, and Manchukuo to Japanese leaders' Diet speeches, as well as Kurusu and Nomura's meetings with Hull and Roosevelt. It describes evacuees arriving aboard the Hikawa Maru and includes Tojo's address to overseas Japanese. A weekly review praises military mobilization and operations in China.

subfiles.title: Hoover cover letter forwarding November 22–30 radio transcripts
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards translated Tokyo broadcasts dated November 22–30, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends Berle translated Tokyo radio transcripts for information.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 22, 1941
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese military, diplomatic, and economic developments and comments on the Diet emergency session.
subfiles.summary: News items cover operations in China, national service rules, an aircraft plant, an air route, and Japanese diplomacy in Thailand and Washington. A commentary presents the Diet session as clarifying policy, demonstrating national resolve, and strengthening finances despite the Allied asset freeze.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 22, 1941, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the November 22 news and commentary on Japanese policy and finances.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the November 22 transcript, including reports on China, Thailand, and Washington and a commentary defending Japan's economic strength.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 22, 1941, third copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the November 22 broadcast's news and account of the Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Third copy of the November 22 transcript, again reporting regional war news and arguing that Japan can withstand economic sanctions.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 23, 1941
subfiles.about: Covers domestic observances and regional news before a long commentary on Japan's economy.
subfiles.summary: The news includes the Harvest Festival, mobilization, reports from China, and ongoing talks in Washington. A lengthy commentary claims Japan has the financial strength and resources to endure an economic blockade. An inserted note disputes the broadcast's claims about coal production and describes shortages and sabotage.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 25, 1941
subfiles.about: Reports a National Support Society rally and transcribes Tojo's speech on national solidarity.
subfiles.summary: Reports speeches at Hibiya Civic Auditorium, the Anti-Comintern Pact anniversary, Japanese-American discussions, and war news. Tojo's transcribed address urges cooperation with government policy, sacrifice, thrift, and resistance to profiteering.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 29, 1941
subfiles.about: Concentrates on the crisis in Japanese-American negotiations after Hull's November 26 note.
subfiles.summary: The broadcast surveys Japanese newspaper reactions, Roosevelt's meetings, developments in China, and European and North African war news. Its extended commentary treats Hull's note as a possible turning point, describes Allied consultations, and insists that Japan's stated demands remain firm.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, November 30, 1941
subfiles.about: Marks the anniversary of Japanese agreements with the Nanjing government amid worsening Pacific diplomacy.
subfiles.summary: Reports anniversary statements by Tojo, Wang Jingwei, and others, together with celebrations of Japanese cooperation with Manchukuo and the Nanjing government. The broadcast blames the United States for stalled negotiations, gives additional war news, and comments at length on the Nanjing government's political and military development.

subfiles.title: Hoover cover letter forwarding December 20–25 radio transcripts
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards translated Tokyo broadcasts dated December 20–25, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends Berle another group of translated Tokyo radio transcripts.

subfiles.title: Station JZI program, December 20, 1941
subfiles.about: Claims Japanese advances at Hong Kong and reports other Pacific War operations.
subfiles.summary: The broadcast predicts Hong Kong's fall, describes attacks in the Philippines and Malaya, and claims heavy American and British naval losses. It stresses Hong Kong's strategic value and notes interference on the recording.
